symptom: `if trim($Value) != empty` passed `check --references`, `exec` and `mx check`, and was always true: a blank or empty value took the 'has text' branch and crashed later in the flow.
cause: Not an mxcli write defect — a platform semantics gap. Mendix String functions (trim, toLowerCase, toUpperCase, substring, replaceAll, toString) return '' for an empty input, never empty, so the comparison is constant. exprcheck had no rule for it; the expression is well-typed, so no kind check could see it.
insight: Settled by measurement, not by reading docs: probe microflows run as `mxcli test --local --db-type hsqldb` on a fresh `mxcli new` 10.18.5 app (no Postgres needed), each classifying f(x) as EMPTY / '' / text for x in empty, '', blanks — with the bare variable as the control that DOES compare equal to empty. The same probe found `empty + ''` is the text 'null'; that one is a pitfalls entry, not a warning, because whether an operand is empty is not knowable at check time. Warn only on measured functions.
